newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's TV3 to launch new free-to-air channel in 1997.
newsitem.headline: NZ's TV3 to launch new free-to-air channel in 1997.

text.p: New Zealand's TV3 Network Ltd said on Wednesday it would form a second free-to-air television channel in mid-1997 to be named TV4.

Managing director Graeme Hunter told a news conference it would be an entertainment-focused channel and broadcast on VHF, ensuring most viewers would be able to receive the signal without making changes to existing aerials.
Hunter said the new channel would broadcast for up to 12 hours a day, seven days a week and it was designed to provide viewers with more programming choice.

"By reorganising the way we use our existing VHF frequency we are now able to create a new free-to-air television channel which will be received by over 60 percent of New Zealanders from day one," Hunter said.
TV3 is controlled by Canada's CanWest Global Communications Corp .
